note: The Art. 14(7) cascade is transcribed from the regulation and is authoritative. The per-state coordinator directory is NOT in the CRA — CSIRTs are designated nationally — so every coordinator is null until a source is read and recorded. A null coordinator means NOT YET SOURCED. It must render as unresolved: the reporting obligation exists regardless of whether we have located the end-point, and showing an unsourced state as 'no body' would convert our own research gap into an apparent absence of obligation.

primary.test: The Member State where decisions related to the cybersecurity of the manufacturer's products with digital elements are predominantly taken.
Where that Member State cannot be determined, the Member State in which the manufacturer has the establishment with the highest number of employees in the Union.

fallbackWhenNoUnionEstablishment.test: The Member State in which the authorised representative acting on behalf of the manufacturer for the highest number of products is established.
The Member State in which the importer placing on the market the highest number of products is established.
The Member State in which the distributor making available on the market the highest number of products is established.
The Member State in which the highest number of users are located.

benchmarkRegimes.name: United Kingdom
benchmarkRegimes.rationale: London-market underwriters benchmark secure-lifecycle and 24h-notification practice against the CRA; the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill trails a similar philosophy. No CRA body is owed a report.
benchmarkRegimes.source: operator assertion 2026-08-22 — NOT independently verified; treat as a recorded judgement, not a finding

benchmarkRegimes.name: United States
benchmarkRegimes.rationale: US underwriters cannot separate domestic from EU risk for manufacturers selling into Europe, and use CRA SBOM/dependency-tracking expectations when assessing standard of care. No CRA body is owed a report.

benchmarkRegimes.name: Australia
benchmarkRegimes.rationale: APAC insurers reportedly require a CRA-framed gap assessment before extending global product-liability cover; domestic policies are said not to cover EU regulatory enforcement costs. No CRA body is owed a report.

benchmarkRegimes.name: Singapore
benchmarkRegimes.rationale: Export-driven risk profile; same underwriting benchmarking as AU. No CRA body is owed a report.

benchmarkRegimes.name: Switzerland
benchmarkRegimes.rationale: Reinsurance hub; global reinsurers are said to prefer uniform CRA-derived product categories for modelling systemic supply-chain risk. No CRA body is owed a report.

benchmarkRegimes.name: Bermuda
benchmarkRegimes.rationale: Reinsurance hub; as CH. No CRA body is owed a report.
